clue.text: It lets you in the moment it's spoken

indicators.note: spoken tells us the words are heard rather than read, so we want a word that sounds like them

parts.note: a moment is a tick, as in 'just a tick', followed by 'it'

explanation.surface: Something that grants entry the instant a password is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' signals a sound-alike: 'tick it' (a moment plus it) said aloud gives the pass to a show or train.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass for a show, train or match is what gets the holder through the door.

clue.text: The enemy has lots of money for an explosive device.

parts.note: time is 'the old enemy'
a bomb is British slang for a large sum, as in 'cost a bomb'

explanation.surface: A hostile force has a fortune to spend on a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is time, as in the saying; 'a bomb' is British slang for a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb set to go off at a fixed hour is a type of explosive device.

clue.text: Horse not such a thoroughbred, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that sounds like the preceding phrase

parts.note: less refined means coarser

explanation.surface: A horse of humbler breeding than a thoroughbred.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift horse, especially a war or hunting steed, is a poetic word for a mount.

clue.text: Begged to eat tender stew

indicators.note: stew means the letters are mixed up as in a pot

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to be fed a tender casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' rearranges EAT TENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech someone earnestly is to plead or beg.

clue.text: Friendly man, perhaps, but one to spread lies

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to slander is to spread malicious falsehoods about someone

explanation.surface: A genial fellow who turns out to be a malicious gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friendly' is not an adjective for kindness: the Friendly Islands are the old name for Tonga, and 'man' hints at the Isle of Man too, so a native of either fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Friendly Islands (Tonga), or of the Isle of Man, is an example of someone born on an island.

clue.text: Tenders contract for plant

parts.note: shepherds tend sheep
to purse the lips is to contract them

explanation.surface: Bids submitted for a factory contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenders' and 'contract' suggest business bids; they are sheep minders and a verb for puckering.
explanation.definitionFit: A common weed of the cabbage family with purse-shaped seed pods.

clue.text: Country has a popular uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry, uprising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mass as in mass appeal means popular

explanation.surface: A nation is in the grip of a people's revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns only the word for popular, read bottom to top in this down entry. Assam is a state of India famed for tea, loosely a country here.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea-growing region of north-east India is a land or territory.

clue.text: Flower that twines round doors, for example.

indicators.note: twines round means the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A climbing plant winding around doorways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower that twines' suggests a climber as the definition, but 'twines round' is the anagram signal and the flower is just 'Flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild rose of hedgerows is a common flower.

clue.text: Get back from a second shot

definitions.meaning: a repeated take of a film scene

explanation.surface: Recovering something by trying again.
explanation.definitionFit: Recapturing a town and refilming a scene are both expressed by the one word.

clue.text: Clergyman depresses us with uncanonical text

indicators.note: in a down entry, the clergyman pressing down on us means he sits above it

parts.note: an ecclesiastic is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A gloomy priest gets everyone down by preaching from a dubious book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depresses' suggests gloom, but in a down clue it means sitting on top of. Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) is in the Apocrypha, hence 'uncanonical'.
explanation.definitionFit: This book of wisdom belongs to the Apocrypha, outside the Hebrew canon, so it is a non-canonical scripture.

clue.text: Growth is bound to give pain, even though there's nothing in it

indicators.note: 'there's nothing in it' tells us the word for nothing sits inside the preceding word

parts.note: is bound to means must
nothing is zero, the letter O
to give pain is to ache

explanation.surface: A doom-laden remark that something is sure to hurt even though it is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even though there's nothing in it' reads as a dismissal but places O inside MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is a facial growth.

clue.text: It helps one shoot a scene

definitions.meaning: the aiming device on a gun or rifle

explanation.surface: A film director's aid for capturing a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests filming, which ties to 'scene', but it is firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's aiming device and a spectacle worth seeing share the one word.

clue.text: Biographer not using all his chief source

indicators.note: not using all of the word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chief is a boss
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A biographer who has not drawn fully on his main informant.
explanation.walkthrough: James Boswell wrote the celebrated Life of Samuel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell is famous as the writer of the life of Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: Call attention discreetly to way of securing poison.

parts.note: to hem is to give a little cough ('ahem') to attract notice
a lock is a means of fastening something

explanation.surface: A hint about how to keep the poison safely locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant extract that killed Socrates is a classic toxin.

clue.text: Married to a traitor, was his death clean?

parts.note: a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: A question about a man wed to a traitor and how he died.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat, the French revolutionary, was stabbed in his bath by Charlotte Corday, hence the joke about a 'clean' death.
explanation.definitionFit: The French revolutionary leader was murdered while bathing, so his death happened in a tub of water.

clue.text: Woman revealing the way to find undiscovered murderer

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
Jack the Ripper, the Victorian killer who was never identified

explanation.surface: A woman uncovers the route to an unsolved killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealing' sounds like exposing a secret, but it means taking off clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who undresses for an audience is revealing herself, the job of a performer at a strip show.

clue.text: Joke's over with this assault course

parts.note: a punch is a blow, an assault
a line is a course or route

explanation.surface: Laughs end when people tackle the obstacle course.
explanation.definitionFit: The final gag that ends a story is where the laugh comes.

clue.text: Binding head broken by gash

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: a rent is a tear or gash

explanation.surface: A bandage on a head wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges HEAD to ADHE, set beside RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adherent sticks fast, so it holds or attaches.

clue.text: Weight-lifter's empty words to girl

parts.note: wind means idle talk, hot air
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder offering hollow flattery to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weight-lifter' suggests an athlete, but it is a winch for hauling loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch with a drum and rope is a machine for hoisting heavy loads.

clue.text: Terrible man, till Scott romanticised him

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible, tsar of Russia
to hoe is to till soil

explanation.surface: A fearsome man until a novelist softened his image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till' looks like 'until' but is the verb to cultivate.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight Wilfred of Ivanhoe is the hero of Walter Scott's romance.

clue.text: Traveller's order is to go in and out

indicators.note: is to go in tells us the order is placed within the other letters
out means the letters of 'and' are rearranged

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: An instruction to a traveller to keep coming and going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AND into NAD, and 'is to go in' sets the Order of Merit inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home is a roaming traveller.

clue.text: You see the fat about at this resort

indicators.note: about means one word is placed around the other

parts.note: marge is British slang for margarine, a cooking fat

explanation.surface: Seaside fry-ups seen everywhere at a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGE is everyday British for margarine. Margate is a seaside resort in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent seaside town is a holiday destination.

clue.text: Permit old composer to put on a little weight

indicators.note: to put on, as clothing, means the composer is wrapped in the letters

parts.note: CT abbreviates carat, a small unit of weight
Thomas Arne, the 18th-century English composer

explanation.surface: Allowing an elderly musician to gain a bit of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: A customs document allowing goods or a vehicle across a border is a type of licence.

clue.text: Architect, a busy creature, not…, accepting requests

parts.note: Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish architect
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: An architect toiling away while refusing all requests.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unyielding will not give way to entreaties.

clue.text: Allow many into passageway.

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal mine passage
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

explanation.surface: Letting a crowd through a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone in is to grant entry.

clue.text: Run with shoe undone — cause a tumble

indicators.note: undone means the letters are taken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner whose shoelace comes undone and trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' rearranges the letters of RUN and SHOE.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a rider from the saddle is to make them fall.

clue.text: Lenin — a humourless prophet, it appears

indicators.note: it appears says the answer shows up within the run of words before

explanation.surface: Lenin portrayed as a joyless seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Project size of crowd when holding single rate

indicators.note: holding means the first words contain the next one

parts.note: to cast is to throw or project
the gate is the attendance at a sporting event
single is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Estimating the crowd figure at a flat price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate' here is the verb meaning to scold, not a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone in the old sense is to scold them severely.

clue.text: Formal account of oral contracts

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so a word that sounds like the next one is wanted

parts.note: treaties are agreements between states

explanation.surface: An official record of verbal agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral contracts' looks like a legal phrase, but 'oral' signals a sound-alike of TREATIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic written discourse on a subject is a formal account of it.

clue.text: Fellow in cap robbed

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a beret is a soft cap

explanation.surface: A fellow in a cap has been robbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deprived of something is being left without it.
